newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania to introduce repo auctions.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania to introduce repo auctions.

text.p: Lithuania's central bank on Thursday said that it planned to start carrying out repo and reverse repo auctions in some one and half months as it takes on more powers to influence monetary policy and the money market.
"These auctions could be held no earlier than in one to one and half months time," central bank monetary policy chief Gintanas Nauseda told Reuters.

The moves come as part of the bank's plans to end the currency board system under which Lithuania's litas is pegged at four to one dollar. It has said it will keep the peg and start open market operations.
The currency board backs the litas as any rise in local currency in circulation has to be matched by a rise in foreign currency reserves.
The system also deprives the bank of any tools to influence monetary policy.

"We intend to apply monetary policy measures in a very careful way, after careful consideration and after we have analysed the needs of commercial banks and a concrete strategy has been estalished," Nauseda added.
He said that the repo and reverse repo auctions would be carried out within the limits set under the currency board.
The central bank has said the end of the currency board will take place gradually, with the bank assuming more powers as the board continues to exist.
It has also repeatedly dimissed talk of a devaluation of the litas from the current four to one rate and said any change in the peg will not come before 1999.
